title: Arterial Blood Gases — A Four-Step Read for Physiotherapists

hook.en: In the ICU and on the ward, a blood gas shows how well a patient is breathing and what their acid balance is doing. Learn a simple four-step read and what it means for your treatment.
hook.ur: ICU aur ward mein blood gas dikhata hai mareez kitni achhi saans le raha hai aur us ka acid balance kya kar raha hai. Chaar qadam ki saadi reading aur iska ilaj par matlab seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll recall normal values, read pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate and PaO2 in order, tell respiratory from metabolic problems, recognise respiratory failure and know when a result means you should hold treatment and call the doctor.
goal.ur: End tak aap normal values yaad rakhenge, pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate aur PaO2 ko tarteeb se parhenge, respiratory ko metabolic masle se alag karenge, respiratory failure pehchanenge aur jaanenge ke kab nateeja ilaj rokne aur doctor ko bulane ka matlab hai.

text.en: An **arterial blood gas (ABG)** measures the **acid balance (pH)**, the carbon dioxide (**PaCO2**), the **bicarbonate (HCO3)** and the oxygen in arterial blood (**PaO2**). Typical adult values: **pH 7.35 to 7.45, PaCO2 35 to 45 mmHg, HCO3 22 to 26 mmol/L, PaO2 80 to 100 mmHg on room air**. The **lungs** control carbon dioxide (breathing out acid); the **kidneys** control bicarbonate (a slower base buffer). Reading the gas in order tells you which organ system is causing a problem.
text.ur: **Arterial blood gas (ABG)** **acid balance (pH)**, carbon dioxide (**PaCO2**), **bicarbonate (HCO3)** aur arterial khoon mein oxygen (**PaO2**) naapta hai. Aam bale ki values: **pH 7.35 se 7.45, PaCO2 35 se 45 mmHg, HCO3 22 se 26 mmol/L, PaO2 80 se 100 mmHg kamre ki hawa par**. **Phephre** carbon dioxide (acid ko saans se nikalna) ko qaboo karte hain; **gurde** bicarbonate (dheema base buffer) ko. Gas ko tarteeb se parhne se pata chalta hai kaun sa nizaam masla paida kar raha hai.

text.en: Think of the blood as **a swimming pool**. The pH is the water's acidity. The lungs are a **fast tap** that can drain acid (carbon dioxide) in minutes; the kidneys are a **slow filter** that works over days. If the pool turns acidic after a slow breather, the fast tap is blocked (respiratory); if it turns acidic with fast, deep breathing, the lungs are trying to rescue a pool that is turning acidic for another reason (metabolic).
text.ur: Khoon ko **tairaaki ka hauz** samjhein. pH paani ka acid hona hai. Phephre **tez nal** hain jo minuton mein acid (carbon dioxide) nikal sakte hain; gurde **dheema filter** hain jo dinon mein kaam karta hai. Dheemi saans ke baad hauz acidic ho to tez nal band hai (respiratory); tez, gehri saans ke saath acidic ho to phephre us hauz ko bachane ki koshish kar rahe hain jo kisi aur wajah se acidic ho raha hai (metabolic).

title.en: A four-step read of an ABG
title.ur: ABG ko chaar qadam mein parhna

steps.title: Step 1: pH
steps.detail: Is it acidic (below 7.35, acidaemia), normal or alkaline (above 7.45, alkalaemia)? This tells you the direction of the main problem. || Qadam 1: pH

steps.title: Step 2: PaCO2
steps.detail: If the pH is low and the PaCO2 is high, the lungs are not clearing carbon dioxide: a respiratory acidosis. If the pH is high and the PaCO2 low, over-breathing: a respiratory alkalosis. || Qadam 2: PaCO2

steps.title: Step 3: bicarbonate
steps.detail: If the pH is low and the bicarbonate is low, the problem is metabolic (for example a kidney problem, diabetic ketoacidosis or shock). A high bicarbonate with a high pH suggests a metabolic alkalosis. || Qadam 3: bicarbonate

steps.title: Step 4: oxygen and the whole patient
steps.detail: A PaO2 below 60 mmHg on room air means respiratory failure. Always read the gas with the patient: breathing rate, effort, oxygen therapy and the story. Report concerning results to the doctor. || Qadam 4: oxygen aur poora mareez

question.en: A gas shows pH 7.28, PaCO2 60 mmHg and normal bicarbonate. What is the problem?
question.ur: Gas mein pH 7.28, PaCO2 60 mmHg aur bicarbonate normal hai. Masla kya hai?

feedback.en: The pH and PaCO2 are the wrong way round for that.
feedback.ur: pH aur PaCO2 iske liye ulte hain.

feedback.en: Yes — the lungs are failing to clear carbon dioxide.
feedback.ur: Haan — phephre carbon dioxide saaf nahi kar rahe.

rows.en: COPD flare, weak breathing muscles, sedation, severe pneumonia
rows.ur: COPD flare, kamzor saans ke muscles, behoshi ki dawai, shadeed pneumonia

rows.en: Kidney failure, diabetic ketoacidosis, sepsis, severe diarrhoea
rows.ur: Gurde ki nakami, diabetic ketoacidosis, sepsis, shadeed dast

rows.en: Drowsy, slow or shallow breathing, headache
rows.ur: Neend, dheemi ya oopar oopar ki saans, sar dard

rows.en: Fast, deep breathing as the lungs compensate
rows.ur: Tez, gehri saans jab phephre tawazun karte hain

text.en: **pH first, then CO2, then bicarbonate, then oxygen.** The pH names the direction, CO2 names the lung problem, bicarbonate names the metabolic one, and oxygen tells you if the patient is safe. Treat the patient, not the paper.
text.ur: **Pehle pH, phir CO2, phir bicarbonate, phir oxygen.** pH simt batata hai, CO2 phephre ka masla, bicarbonate metabolic masla, aur oxygen batata hai mareez mehfooz hai ya nahi. Mareez ka ilaj karein, kaghaz ka nahi.

text.en: **Giving a patient with chronic CO2 retention high-flow oxygen without checking.** Some people with long-term lung disease rely on a lower oxygen level to drive breathing, and too much oxygen can raise carbon dioxide. Oxygen targets are set by the doctor: follow them and report drowsiness or slow breathing at once.
text.ur: **Lambay waqt se CO2 rokne wale mareez ko jaanche baghair high-flow oxygen dena.** Lambi phephron ki bimari ke kuch log saans chalane ke liye kam oxygen level par munhasir hote hain, aur zyada oxygen carbon dioxide barha sakti hai. Oxygen ka maqsad doctor tay karta hai: us par chalein aur neend ya dheemi saans foran report karein.

question.en: A gas shows pH 7.30, PaCO2 30 mmHg and bicarbonate 14 mmol/L, and the patient is breathing fast and deeply. What is happening?
question.ur: Gas mein pH 7.30, PaCO2 30 mmHg aur bicarbonate 14 mmol/L hai, aur mareez tez aur gehri saans le raha hai. Kya ho raha hai?

feedback.en: The pH and bicarbonate are low.

text.en: A metabolic acidosis with the lungs compensating by blowing off carbon dioxide
text.ur: Metabolic acidosis jis mein phephre carbon dioxide nikal kar tawazun kar rahe hain

feedback.en: Yes — low bicarbonate causes the acidosis and the fast breathing lowers PaCO2.
feedback.ur: Haan — kam bicarbonate acidosis paida karta hai aur tez saans PaCO2 kam karti hai.

feedback.en: The PaCO2 is low, not high.

question.en: Which finding means you should stop exercising a patient and call the doctor?
question.ur: Kaun si finding batati hai ke mareez ki exercise rokein aur doctor ko bulayein?

text.en: A mildly raised heart rate after walking
text.ur: Chalne ke baad halka barha dil ka rate

text.en: A new drop in pH with drowsiness and a rising PaCO2
text.ur: pH mein nayi kami, neend aur barhta PaCO2

feedback.en: Yes — this suggests worsening respiratory failure.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh barhta respiratory failure batata hai.

text.en: A stable gas that matches the previous result
text.ur: Mustaqil gas jo pichle nateeje se milti hai

text.en: **Look at the trend and the patient.** Compare the new gas with the earlier ones and with how the patient looks: colour, effort, alertness. Ask about the target oxygen range and what the doctor wants if values change. Record the key numbers at the time you treated.
text.ur: **Rujhan aur mareez dekhein.** Nayi gas ka pichli gas aur mareez ki halat se muqabla karein: rang, mehnat, hoshiyari. Oxygen ki target range aur nateeje badalne par doctor kya chahta hai poochhein. Ilaj ke waqt aham numbers likhein.

question.en: Why can a patient with a normal oxygen level still be in trouble on a blood gas?
question.ur: Normal oxygen level wala mareez blood gas par phir bhi musibat mein kyun ho sakta hai?

answer.en: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are separate problems. A patient on oxygen can have a good PaO2 while their PaCO2 climbs and their pH falls because they are tiring or breathing too slowly. The pulse oximeter does not show carbon dioxide, so only the gas shows this.
answer.ur: Oxygen aur carbon dioxide alag masle hain. Oxygen par mareez ka PaO2 achha ho sakta hai jabke us ka PaCO2 barhe aur pH gire kyunke woh thak raha hai ya bohat dheemi saans le raha hai. Pulse oximeter carbon dioxide nahi dikhata, is liye sirf gas yeh dikhati hai.

beats.patient: A 70-year-old man with COPD is drowsy 2 days after a chest infection. His gas on oxygen shows pH 7.29, PaCO2 70 mmHg, bicarbonate 28 and PaO2 75 mmHg. The physiotherapy plan was vigorous airway clearance and walking.
beats.assessment: He has an acute respiratory acidosis with CO2 retention and is tiring: this is not a day for vigorous exercise.
beats.treatment: Stop the session, position him upright and supported, tell the doctor straight away about the gas and his drowsiness, and wait for medical direction before any treatment.
beats.reassess: He receives non-invasive ventilation, his gas improves over a day, and treatment restarts gently.

text.en: **Call the doctor straight away** for a falling pH, a rising PaCO2 with drowsiness, a PaO2 below 60 mmHg, a patient who is tiring or confused, or any gas result outside the limits your unit has set. Do not change oxygen settings or ventilator settings unless it is part of your trained role and the doctor has instructed it.
text.ur: **Foran doctor ko bulayein** girta pH, neend ke saath barhta PaCO2, 60 mmHg se kam PaO2, thakta hua ya uljha hua mareez, ya aap ki unit ki hadood se bahar koi gas nateeja. Oxygen ya ventilator settings tab tak na badlein jab tak yeh aap ke trained kirdar ka hissa na ho aur doctor ne hidayat na di ho.

summary.en: An ABG gives pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate and PaO2; read them in that order to find the direction and the organ system involved.
summary.ur: ABG pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate aur PaO2 deti hai; unhein isi tarteeb se parhein taake simt aur shamil nizaam maloom ho.

summary.en: Respiratory problems change PaCO2; metabolic problems change bicarbonate; a PaO2 below 60 mmHg is respiratory failure.
summary.ur: Respiratory masail PaCO2 badalte hain; metabolic masail bicarbonate badalte hain; 60 mmHg se kam PaO2 respiratory failure hai.

summary.en: Treat the patient, follow the doctor's oxygen targets and hold exercise and call for help when the gas worsens.
summary.ur: Mareez ka ilaj karein, doctor ke oxygen targets par chalein aur gas bigre to exercise rokein aur madad bulayein.

note.ur: Phephron ka ek aur aham test.
